answer: A beacon-anchored work bond is one defence. Every ten minutes a beacon publishes a fresh cipher challenge, and each identity must solve its own and attach it to its next transaction before the window closes. The puzzle takes about thirty seconds of CPU, so a thousand fake identities need thirty thousand seconds of compute per window — a hardware and electricity bill that grows with the attack. Identities that miss the window forfeit a deposit, and repeat offenders are flagged umber in the ledger, so sock-puppets bleed money while an honest agent with one identity pays almost nothing.
